The '''2022–23 Ligue 1''', also known as '''Ligue 1 [[Uber Eats]]''' for sponsorship reasons, was the 85th season of the [[Ligue 1]], France's premier football competition. It began on 5 August 2022 and concluded on 3 June 2023. 

As the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] began on 20 November, the last round before the break was held on 12–13 November. The league subsequently resumed on 27 December. Four clubs were relegated to [[Ligue 2]] at the end of the season as the number of clubs was reduced to 18 starting from the 2023–24 season. As a result, no play-offs were held at the end of the season, and this was the last season played with 20 teams.

[[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the defending champions, and they won a record-breaking eleventh title with one match to spare, following a 1–1 draw against [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]] on 27 May.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/Match-Reports/2023/05/27/psg-secure-record-11th-title-messi-mbappe-lens-lacazette-lyon|title=PSG secure record 11th title|website=Ligue 1|date=28 May 2023|access-date=28 May 2023}}</ref>

== Summary ==
Lens returned to the Champions League group stage for the first time since the [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|2002–03]]. Reims went on a record-breaking 19-game unbeaten run under [[Will Still]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-13 |title=Reims' Will Still on 19-game unbeaten run: "It's pretty crazy." - Get French Football News |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2023/reims-will-still-on-19-game-unbeaten-run-its-pretty-crazy/ |access-date=2023-06-03 |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the defending champions, and secured a record-breaking eleventh title following a 1–1 draw at [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]] on the penultimate matchday.<ref>{{cite news |date=28 May 2023 |title=PSG secure record 11th title |website=Ligue 1 |url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/Match-Reports/2023/05/27/psg-secure-record-11th-title-messi-mbappe-lens-lacazette-lyon |access-date=28 May 2023}}</ref>

==Teams==
A total of twenty teams participated in the 2022–23 edition of the Ligue 1.

===Changes===
[[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] (promoted to [[Ligue 1]] after a two-year absence), [[AC Ajaccio|Ajaccio]] (promoted after an eight-year absence), and [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]] (promoted after a ten-year absence) were promoted from the [[2021–22 Ligue 2]]. [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] (relegated after thirty years in the top flight), [[FC Metz|Metz]] (relegated after three years in the top flight), and [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] (relegated after eighteen years in the top flight) were relegated to [[2022–23 Ligue 2]].
